newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday November 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday November 14.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Former magistrate and Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro is said to be under preliminary investigation on charges of corruption (all).

* The Lower House of parliament approved the highly contested articles of the 1997 budget concerning income tax modifications and a new regional tax. The centre-right opposition keeps deserting the parliamentary budget debate in protest at the package and Freedom Alliance leader Silvio Berlusconi says "We are on red alert. The country and its democracy are in serious danger" (all).
* The government won three confidence votes in the Upper House Senate over a rescue plan for Banco di Napoli, and a development project in Naples (all).
* The Pope called on world leaders at the UN sponsored World Food Summit in Rome to bridge the gap beetween rich and poor (all).

* In a meeting with Industry minister Pier Luigi Bersani, trade unions judged positively the planned merger of state telecom holding STET and its operating arm Telecom Italia. STET is expected to be transferred to the Treasury by the end of the year and the merger should take place by next spring (Corriere della Sera, Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Olivetti is said to have "frozen" talks with UK-based Klesch and Co over a possible sale of its ailing PC company, because there is a "better offer" (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* A joint venture between Italy's Ansaldo Energia Spa and US NRG Energy Inc signed an agreement to sell power to Indonesia's state electricity firm PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara. The joint venture will build a 400 megawatt power plant valued at 900 billion lire (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Italian December BTP futures on the LIFFE market hit another record high of 126.62 (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
